examples.en: I did terribly on the exam, so I'm upset.

examples.ko: 어제 경기에서 우리 팀이 형편없이 졌어요.
examples.en: Our team lost badly in yesterday's game.
My cooking skills are awfully clumsy.
The service at that restaurant was terribly bad.
I got rained on, and my clothes got completely soaked.
I went to karaoke after a long time and sang terribly.

explain: '형편없다'의 부사형으로, 뒤에 '지다', '나쁘다', '서툴다'처럼 좋지 않은 말이 자주 와요. '엉망으로'와 비슷하지만 수준이 매우 낮다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 명사 앞에서는 '형편없는'을 써요.

phrases.en: My cooking skills are pretty terrible.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서는 '형편없는'으로 바꿔 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun, change it to 'hyeongpyeoneopsneun'.

phrases.en: My score on this test is terribly low.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낮다'처럼 수준이 좋지 않다는 말과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with words about a poor level, like 'nat-da'.

phrases.en: Today's game result is really awful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서술어로 쓰는 기본형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The base predicate form.

explain_en: This is the adverb form of '형편없다', and it is often followed by negative words like '지다' (lose), '나쁘다', and '서툴다'. It resembles '엉망으로' (in a mess), but feels more like the level is extremely low. Before a noun, use '형편없는'.

en: to be verified; to be proven

examples.ko: 이 방법은 이미 여러 번 검증됐어요.
examples.en: This method has already been verified many times.
We only sell products whose safety has been verified.
That rumor hasn't been verified yet.

examples.ko: 실력이 검증되면 정식 직원이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Once your skills are verified, you can become a regular employee.
A new theory is verified through experiments.
Let's wait until the effect is verified.

explain: 사실인지 맞는지를 확인하는 과정을 거쳐서 믿을 만하다고 인정받은 상태를 말해요. '증명되다'는 옳다는 것이 확실히 보인 결과이고, '검증되다'는 확인 절차를 통과한 거예요. 광고나 리뷰에서 '검증된 제품'이라는 말을 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: I only buy verified products.
phrases.nuance_ko: '검증되다'를 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태로, 광고나 리뷰에서 아주 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun; very common in ads and reviews.

phrases.en: That rumor hasn't been verified yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 확인 절차를 아직 통과하지 못했다고 말할 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when something hasn't yet passed checking.

phrases.example: 이 약은 여러 번 검증을 거쳤어요.
phrases.en: This medicine went through verification many times.
phrases.nuance_ko: '검증되다'보다 확인하는 과정을 지나왔다는 점을 더 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Puts more focus on the process of going through checks than 검증되다 does.

explain_en: It describes something that passed a process of checking whether it is true or correct and is accepted as reliable. 증명되다 is the result of being shown to be right; 검증되다 means it passed verification. You often see '검증된 제품' in ads and reviews.

gh: shown true by logic or proof

p.n: 검증 means it was checked by testing; 증명 means it was shown true.

t90.ax: That rumor hasn't been verified yet.

examples.en: The survey results are analyzed in a table.
The cause has not been analyzed yet.
We held a meeting after looking at the analyzed data.
The sample will be analyzed tomorrow.

examples.ko: 이 사고는 여러 가지로 분석되고 있어요.
examples.en: This accident is being analyzed in several ways.
The data was analyzed and came out as a graph.

explain: '분석하다'는 사람이 하는 일이고, '분석되다'는 결과나 자료가 주인공일 때 써요. 뉴스, 보고서, 연구 글에서 자주 나와요. '결과가 분석되다'처럼 말하면 누가 했는지는 말하지 않아요.

phrases.en: The survey data is analyzed in detail.
phrases.nuance_ko: '자세히' 같은 부사로 분석 방법을 더해 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adverbs like 자세히 describe how the analysis is done.

phrases.en: The results are being analyzed now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 진행 중인 분석을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for analysis that is happening now.

phrases.en: I wrote the analyzed results in the report.
phrases.nuance_ko: '분석된 + 명사'로 이미 분석이 끝난 것을 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: '분석된 + noun' describes something already analyzed.

explain_en: Use the active verb when a person does the analyzing, and this passive form when the data or result is the subject. It shows up in news, reports, and research writing, and it leaves out who did the work.

examples.en: A picture is presented in the exam.
A new opinion was put forward at the meeting.
The price is shown on the website.
Answer according to the conditions given.

examples.ko: 좋은 방법이 제시되면 따라 해 볼게요.
examples.en: If a good method is put forward, I will try it.
The correct answer was not given in the question.

explain: 시험, 회의, 안내문에서 어떤 내용이 눈앞에 내밀어질 때 써요. 내가 보여 주면 '제시하다'예요. 신분증이나 표를 보여 달라고 할 때는 '제시해 주세요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Look at the picture shown and talk about it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시험 문제에서 자주 보는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen in exam questions.

phrases.en: A way to solve the problem was presented.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회의나 글에서 생각이나 방법이 내밀어졌다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means an idea or method was put forward in a meeting or text.

phrases.en: The answers are given below the question.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 있다'로 이미 보이게 놓여 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of already being displayed.

explain_en: It is used in exams, meetings and notices when some content is put in front of you. When you present it, use '제시하다'. When asked to show an ID or ticket, the phrase is '제시해 주세요'.

examples.ko: 이 장치는 연기를 탐지해서 경보를 울려요.
examples.en: This device detects smoke and sounds an alarm.
Dogs detect drugs by smell.
The radar detected a small boat.

examples.ko: 문제를 일찍 탐지하면 큰 피해를 막을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you detect a problem early, you can prevent big damage.
I installed a program that detects computer viruses.

examples.ko: 지진을 미리 탐지할 수 있는 기술이 필요해요.
examples.en: We need technology that can detect earthquakes in advance.

explain: 기계나 장치가 눈에 안 보이는 것을 찾아낼 때 써요. 사람이 눈으로 찾으면 '발견하다', 몰래 알아보는 일은 '알아내다'를 더 많이 써요. 보통 '연기를 탐지하다', '이상 징후를 탐지하다'처럼 대상이 숨어 있는 것이에요.

phrases.en: Gas was detected inside the house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨은 것이 찾아졌다는 결과를 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, stating the result that something hidden was found.

phrases.example: 이 기계는 작은 움직임도 탐지할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This machine can detect even small movements.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계의 능력을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to explain what a machine can do.

phrases.en: The system detected a sign that something was wrong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 생기기 전의 작은 신호를 찾아낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for finding small warning signs before a problem happens.

explain_en: Use it when a device finds something you can't see directly. When a person finds it by eye, Koreans say 발견하다; for quietly finding out, 알아내다 is more common. The object is usually something hidden, such as 연기를 탐지하다 or 이상 징후를 탐지하다 (detect a warning sign).

examples.en: There is less oxygen at high altitude, so I get out of breath.
Winter comes early in the highlands.

examples.ko: 그 마을은 고산에 있어서 길이 가팔라요.
examples.en: That village is high in the mountains, so the roads are steep.
Alpine plants withstand the cold well.
I had a headache because of altitude sickness.

examples.ko: 해발 삼천 미터가 넘는 고산을 오르는 게 꿈이에요.
examples.en: My dream is to climb a high mountain over three thousand meters.

explain: '고산'은 '고산병', '고산 식물', '고산 지대'처럼 다른 말과 합쳐서 자주 써요. 산 하나를 가리킬 때는 그냥 '산'이나 '높은 산'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I got altitude sickness after climbing a high mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 곳에서 몸이 아픈 병을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The sickness caused by high places.

phrases.example: 이 꽃은 고산 식물이라서 추운 곳에서 잘 자라요.
phrases.en: This flower is an alpine plant, so it grows well in cold places.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 산에서 자라는 식물을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Plants that grow on high mountains.

phrases.en: Tibet is in a high-altitude region.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 땅이 넓게 있는 지역을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A region with wide high-altitude land.

explain_en: '고산' is mostly used in compounds like '고산병', '고산 식물' and '고산 지대'. To point to a single mountain, people just say '산' or '높은 산'.

examples.en: Stars can be observed well in the night sky.
A strange change was observed in the experiment.

examples.ko: 이 새는 겨울에 주로 관찰되곤 해요.
examples.en: This bird is mainly seen in winter.

examples.ko: 작은 곤충의 움직임이 현미경으로 관찰되니까 신기해요.
examples.en: It's amazing that you can see the tiny insect's movement through the microscope.
If there are noticeable symptoms, go to the hospital.
No snow was observed this month.

explain: '관찰하다'는 사람이 자세히 보는 일이고, '관찰되다'는 '눈에 띄게 보인다'는 결과를 말해요. 과학, 뉴스, 보고서에서 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '보이다'를 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: You can see the stars well from here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word more often used in daily talk.

phrases.en: I wrote the observed results in a table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자세히 본 뒤 알게 된 내용을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for what was found after careful observation.

phrases.en: This bird is easily observed in spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어렵지 않게 볼 수 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it can be seen without difficulty.

explain_en: 관찰하다 is a person watching carefully, while 관찰되다 states that something is seen or noticed. It is common in science, news and reports. In everyday talk, 보이다 is used more often.

examples.en: A variety of minerals are found in this area.
I looked at the sparkling minerals at the museum.

examples.ko: 광물 중에는 휴대폰을 만드는 데 쓰이는 것도 있어요.
examples.en: Some minerals are used to make cell phones.
I heard this cosmetic is made from natural minerals.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 광물의 단단한 정도를 비교했어요.
examples.en: In science class we compared the hardness of minerals.

examples.ko: 광물 채취는 허가를 받아야만 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only collect minerals with a permit.

explain: 금·철·돌 같은 땅속 자연물을 말해요. 영양제의 '미네랄'은 몸에 필요한 성분이라서, 학교 과학이나 지질에서는 광물, 건강 이야기에서는 미네랄이라고 해요. 돈이 되는 금속 재료는 '광석'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: This country is rich in mineral resources.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라나 지역이 가진 땅속 재료를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for underground materials that a country or region has.

phrases.en: Miners dig minerals out of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅속에서 꺼내는 일을 말할 때 '캐다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 캐다 for taking minerals out of the ground.

phrases.en: Iron is taken from ore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광물 중에서 금속을 얻을 수 있는 돌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to rock from which metal can be extracted.

explain_en: It refers to natural substances in the ground, such as gold, iron, and stones. The 미네랄 in supplements is the nutrient the body needs, so school science and geology use 광물 while health talk uses 미네랄. The raw material worth refining into metal is also called 광석.

t90.ax: Some minerals are used to make cell phones.

examples.en: When I cut the tree, the annual rings were clearly visible.

examples.ko: 나이테를 세어 보면 나무가 몇 살인지 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you count the rings, you can tell how old the tree is.

examples.ko: 이 나무는 나이테 간격이 아주 촘촘해요.
examples.en: This tree's rings are very close together.
The rings remain as circles on the stump.
The teacher showed us a photo of tree rings.
One more ring is added every year.

explain: 나무 이야기에만 쓰고 사람 나이에는 쓰지 않아요. 한자어로 '연륜'이라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '나이테'를 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: This tree has thick growth rings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무가 빨리 자란 해에는 나이테가 굵다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Rings are thick in years when the tree grew fast.

phrases.en: A tree gets one new ring every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해마다 늘어나는 모습을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain how rings are added each year.

phrases.example: 나무의 나이테를 보면 날씨도 알 수 있어요.
phrases.en: From a tree's rings you can also learn about the weather.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나무의'를 앞에 붙여 대상을 분명히 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 나무의 makes clear what it belongs to.

explain_en: It is used only for trees, never for a person's age. The Sino-Korean word '연륜' also exists, but in daily life 나이테 is more common.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 농경지가 넓게 펼쳐져 있어요.
examples.en: Farmland stretches widely across this area.
The farmland was flooded because of the flood.

examples.ko: 도시가 커지면서 농경지가 점점 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: As the city grows, farmland is shrinking little by little.
The government announced a policy to protect farmland.
It's a place where they cut into a mountain to make farmland.
Looking down from the plane, the farmland looked like a checkerboard.

explain: 뉴스나 서류에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 말할 때는 '논밭'이나 '농지'라고 해요. '농경지가 줄어들다'처럼 땅의 넓이를 이야기할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Farmland around here is expensive.
phrases.nuance_ko: '농경지'와 뜻은 같지만 조금 짧고 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 농경지 but shorter and more common.

phrases.en: There are wide rice paddies and fields around the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 논과 밭을 함께 부르는 말로, 말할 때 가장 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means rice paddies and fields together; the most natural in speech.

phrases.en: Farmland is shrinking as the city grows.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 땅의 넓이가 변하는 이야기를 할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the news when talking about changes in land area.

explain_en: It is a stiff word for news and documents. In speech people say 논밭 or 농지. It often appears when discussing land area, as in 농경지가 줄어들다.

t90.ax: Farmland stretches widely across this area.

en: to be distributed; to range; to be found (across an area)

examples.ko: 이 식물은 따뜻한 지역에 많이 분포해요.
examples.en: This plant is widely found in warm regions.
Penguins are found mainly in the Southern Hemisphere.

examples.ko: 전국에 분포하는 가게라서 어디서나 찾을 수 있어요.
examples.en: It's a chain spread across the country, so you can find it anywhere.

examples.ko: 이 곤충은 산에만 분포해서 도시에서는 보기 어려워요.
examples.en: This insect lives only in mountains, so it's hard to see in cities.

examples.ko: 인구가 한곳에만 분포하지 않고 넓게 퍼져 있어요.
examples.en: The population isn't concentrated in one place but spread out widely.

examples.ko: 이 새가 분포하는 지역을 지도에 표시했어요.
examples.en: I marked the areas where this bird is found on the map.

explain: 동식물이나 사람, 가게가 어떤 범위에 퍼져 있는 모습을 과학이나 통계 글에서 말할 때 써요. 일상에서는 '살다', '퍼져 있다'가 더 자연스러워요. '나이 분포', '지역 분포'처럼 명사 '분포'로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: This bird is found widely across Asia.
phrases.nuance_ko: '널리'와 함께 쓰면 넓은 범위에 퍼져 있다는 뜻이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '널리' it clearly means something is spread over a wide area.

phrases.example: 이 나무는 산 위쪽에 분포하고 있어요.
phrases.en: These trees are found in the upper part of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 있다'를 붙이면 지금 그렇게 퍼져 있는 상태를 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-고 있다' it describes the current state of how something is spread out.

phrases.example: 인구가 나라 전체에 고르게 분포하지 않아요.
phrases.en: The population is not evenly distributed across the country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고르게'와 '않다'를 붙여 한곳에 몰려 있다는 말을 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '고르게' with a negative to say that something is concentrated in one place.

explain_en: Used in science or statistics to describe how animals, plants, people or shops are spread over an area. In daily speech 살다 or 퍼져 있다 sounds more natural. The noun 분포 is also common, as in 나이 분포 (age distribution).

t90.ax: This plant is widely found in warm regions.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 삼림이 잘 보존되어 있어요.
examples.en: The forests in this region are well preserved.
A lot of forest was lost to the wildfire.

examples.ko: 삼림을 지키려면 나무를 함부로 베면 안 돼요.
examples.en: To protect the forest, you must not cut trees carelessly.
I breathed clean air in the woods.
Many animals live in forest areas.

examples.ko: 삼림 자원을 아껴 쓰는 일이 중요해요.
examples.en: Using forest resources carefully is important.

explain: 일상에서 쓰는 순우리말은 '숲'이고, '삼림'은 뉴스나 교과서에서 넓은 숲을 말할 때 쓰는 한자어예요. 산책하며 말할 때는 '숲'이 자연스러워요. '산림'도 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.en: Protecting forests is important.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삼림'과 거의 같은 뜻이고, 나라가 관리하는 숲 이야기에 더 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 삼림; more common when talking about managed forests.

phrases.example: 삼림 보호를 위해 나무를 많이 심어요.
phrases.en: We plant many trees to protect the forests.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 환경 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase in news and environmental talk.

phrases.en: Forests are shrinking because of development.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숲의 넓이가 점점 작아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the area of forest keeps getting smaller.

explain_en: The everyday native word is '숲', while '삼림' is a Sino-Korean word used in news and textbooks for large woodlands. On a walk, '숲' sounds natural. '산림' is used in almost the same way.

t90.ax: I breathed clean air in the woods.

examples.en: In science class, I learned that frogs are amphibians.

examples.ko: 양서류는 물과 땅 양쪽에서 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: Amphibians can live both in water and on land.
I heard that salamanders are also amphibians.
I observed several amphibians at this pond.

examples.ko: 환경이 변하면 양서류가 먼저 영향을 받는대요.
examples.en: They say amphibians are affected first when the environment changes.
In class, I gave a presentation on the differences between reptiles and amphibians.

explain: 개구리, 도롱뇽처럼 어릴 때는 물에서 살고 자라면 땅에서도 사는 동물의 무리를 말해요. 주로 과학 수업이나 설명에 나오고, 뱀이나 도마뱀 같은 '파충류'와 구분해서 말해요.

phrases.en: There are many amphibians like frogs.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동물'을 붙여 이 무리에 속하는 동물을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 동물 points to animals that belong to this group.

phrases.en: Amphibians and reptiles are different.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷해 보이는 두 무리를 구분할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to tell apart two groups that look alike.

phrases.en: Salamanders belong to the amphibians.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 동물이 이 무리에 들어간다고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain that an animal belongs to this group.

explain_en: It names the group of animals like frogs and salamanders that live in water when young and can live on land as adults. It mostly appears in science classes and explanations, and is contrasted with '파충류' (reptiles) such as snakes and lizards.
